content: {"summary":"After the 19 March 2025 zone push, orders‑api saw intermittent NXDOMAIN because internal‑dns‑01 served a newer zone missing the database record while internal‑dns‑02 still had the older zone. The missing record was re‑added with a higher serial and redeployed to internal‑dns‑01, and once the CoreDNS cache turned over the lookups resolved again.","likely_cause":"Missing DNS record in the zone file on internal‑dns‑01 after the zone push","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"NXDOMAIN responses occurred because internal‑dns‑01 served a newer zone missing the record while internal‑dns‑02 still had the older zone with the record.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#1","INC-0025#2"],"quote":"Only internal-dns-01 served the new file, so a cache period that happened to land there came back NXDOMAIN"},{"text":"The record was re‑added with a higher serial and redeployed to internal‑dns‑01, after which cache turnover restored correct lookups.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#2","INC-0025#3"],"quote":"The record went back into the zone source with a higher serial"},{"text":"After the cache turned over, orders‑api‑02 resolved lookups consistently.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#3"],"quote":"Once the cluster cache turned over, lookups from orders-api-02 resolved every time"}],"next_checks":["Verify zone file serials on both internal‑dns servers after any push","Monitor CoreDNS cache turnover times for DNS changes","Add validation in the rollout tool to confirm zone contents before restart"]}
